name: MCP Host Matrix

scope.subject: Selected MCP host and bridge behavior; mcp-remote is one component, not the entire scope.

os_scope: Linux/WSL2; per-path limits retained in original pages
observations: No revocation request reached the provider in the 12 selected base windows; the prior refresh was accepted by separate controller replay with the required profile credentials.
Logout and Clear authentication controls sent revocation requests; the prior refresh was then refused.
Accepted work, transport, provider authority, registration and local state are distinct.

traffic_example.population: Entire closed VS Code PUBLIC-NODCR journal including baseline

controls: Healthy closed observation windows at least 60 s after observer ACK
Correct same-profile prior-refresh replay before and after the operation
Working logout and Clear authentication revocation controls
limits: Selected operations and profiles; other host operations were not measured.
The test provider let accepted work finish, so completion after transport close alone does not establish a cancellation defect.
Store/process snapshots and exact UI timing have per-case limits.
No attacker path, contract violation, CVE, severity or production impact established.

subcases.path_status: Path not observed within the measured window
subcases.scope: Bearer reuse across ordinary different server URLs
Bearer reuse under a cache-key alias
Usable retained refresh after CLI remove

subcases.path_status: B refresh request observed; no B access issuance observed
subcases.scope: Refresh-resource binding with a qualified A-positive control

subcases.path_status: Inherited permissions on a secondary data drive: read and refresh observed; effective-default-DACL projection: read denied; real default-cache runtime unmeasured
subcases.scope: Cross-SID access to a retained bridge cache under the measured ACL variants

observations: Ordinary different URL: five native B target requests had no A bearer; same-tuple A reuse worked.
Delimiter serialization alias: different same-origin URL/resource inputs produced the same key bytes; B presented A bearer and received HTTP 401. This is not a cryptographic MD5 collision.
Separate A-only same-SID post-remove file reader exchanged the retained refresh and received HTTP 200; file hash and ACL were unchanged.
Qualified resource comparison: A refresh returned HTTP 200 on the same grant before B requested a different explicit resource and received HTTP 400; no new B access or tool call.

Cross-SID file access: inherited permissions on a secondary data drive allowed known-path read and refresh with HTTP 200; the synthetic effective-default-DACL projection denied read with EPERM, no bytes and no HTTP from that reader.
controls: Same-tuple native A OAuth and tool calls
A-positive refresh before B under the qualified resource oracle
Own-readable and private-denied canaries; fresh, invalid, A-after-B and revocation controls
limits: Real default profile metadata only; no runtime access to personal credentials.
Known-path reader, not native B discovery or file-write test.
Final projection logs retain EPERM only; exact stat/read syscall unknown.
Same-origin alias and synthetic grant-resource policy are not arbitrary external recipient/production claims.
The subcases are separate measured paths and do not establish one continuous attack chain.

observations: Same identity and connection: inputSchema A {a: string} changed to B {b: string}, with additionalProperties: false.
A no-change notice triggered reread; fresh native inspect retained schema A. The changed notice produced native schema B.
Valid B reached the server; selected invalid and stale inputs also reached the server and were rejected there.
controls: No-change notification and fresh native inspect
Valid A and valid B calls with the server validator
Wire receipts for invalid and stale calls
limits: Programmatic invokeTool/autoTrustChanges/trust-disabled own workspace, not ordinary UI consent.
No description/set/reconnect/other-host/poisoning protection measurement.
Different runtime/reference protocol versions must remain distinguished.

cases.interception: Own post-init child environment selects an inert recorder executable; package/builtin functions unchanged.
observations: The HTTP metadata URL reached encoded UTF-16LE argv and the inert recorder; image, PID, creation time and exit were correlated.
The unsupported r04-fixture URI produced an explicit sanitizeUrl stack before the opener; no recorder event.
Bridge success was logged while the helper was still running; recorder exit 0 occurred later.
Discovery, URL logging and a callback listener existed before rejection.
controls: Qualified inert-recorder execution with exact identity and event capture
Standalone stock-open exact-target control and other-target matcher rejection
Explicit sanitizer exception and identity, argv and cleanup correspondence
limits: Actual PowerShell parser, browser and URI handler were excluded, not measured.
Positive recorder exited naturally with code 0; positive Node/wrapper were forcibly stopped with code 97 after observation while awaiting callback.
Metadata bodies not separately captured; request/response event records retained.
No-server, affected/fixed and other platform/auth/URI contexts unmeasured.

observations: Origin A token endpoint sent HTTP 307 to a second owned loopback origin B; B captured the same synthetic refresh, client and resource form body in all three automatic attempts.
B returned HTTP 400 invalid_grant; no successful target RPC or new access issuance during the target refresh stage; additional device approval was not granted.
Grant linkage comes from A state and binding checks, not a grant_id field in the B wire body.
controls: Direct valid native refresh returned HTTP 200 and a new-bearer MCP call succeeded
Invalid refresh returned HTTP 400 with no token issuance
A and B health checks; receiver dummy exact-body and PID control
limits: One synthetic PUBLIC-NODCR HTTP 307 case; other redirect, authentication, TLS, issuer and resource combinations were not measured.
B intentionally denied exchange; attacker control of Location and successful real-provider exchange were not established.
Bootstrap access existed; zero refers only to new access issuance during the target refresh stage.
Two ports and four handles were checked; error 10035 was a timeout, not a refusal; idle error 10054 was not an extra request.
The post-trigger missing token file has no attributed deletion actor.

observations: The prior provider authority was accepted in 8 of 8 cells across 4 conceptual rows.
Surviving prior authority and native prior-refresh reuse by the new build were both observed in 2 of 4 rows, in both profiles.
Four bridge cells requested new authorization; four native cells reused the prior refresh and completed tool calls.
Registration, local storage, native first connection and controller replay are separate observations.
controls: Correct prior-refresh replay before and after the update
Wrong-client, wrong-management, revocation and fresh-grant-survival controls where applicable
limits: Native rows used same-path/profile build replacement; bridge rows used explicit-pin or local-latest launch selection. Official installers and built-in auto-updaters were not measured.
Native rows let old access expire naturally under short-TTL synthetic policy; bridge launch selection did not wait for access expiry. Clocks/stores were not edited to force refresh.
Controller replay is separate from native reuse.
After-store snapshots follow at least 60 seconds and controller replay, not immediate first connection.
Encrypted VS Code values were not decrypted.
High VS Code refresh counts are fixture-window observations, not product norms or diagnosed defects.

separate_unmeasured_work: Ordinary UI consent; real default-profile access; native other-SID discovery/write
Other URI, issuer, resource, TLS and authentication contexts
